title: Archel — portfolio design direction
question: Choose the original visual system to develop. All options preserve the confirmed recruiting story and easter eggs.

options.label: Evidence Index
options.thesis: A bold section index frames a readable record of product decisions and outcomes.
options.viewport: Left: numbered section navigation. Center: name, specialization, Projects and Resume. Bottom: three precisely labeled professional outcomes.
options.risk: The index must collapse cleanly on phones and never hide essential evidence.

raised.raise: Selected controls must remain unmistakable without color.
Every destination gets a stable, directly accessible address.
Keep every claim adjacent to its supporting project or context.
Use one consistent alignment grid beneath the expressive framing.
Give active navigation one continuous, restrained motion cue.
Keep dates and metric qualifications attached to their evidence.

options.label: Decision Journal
options.thesis: An editorial opening pairs Archel’s identity with one lead professional case.
options.viewport: Large name and direct actions on the left; payment conversion case on the right; secondary outcomes below.
options.risk: More familiar portfolio composition; navigation carries less of the reference’s personality.

options.label: One-bit desktop
options.risk: Window management adds work to a short recruiting visit.
options.case: Declined: weaker fit for this reference-led recruiting brief on audience identification and immediate product clarity.

options.label: Teletext
options.risk: Bitmap density and page-key input weaken quick reading.
options.case: Declined: weaker fit for this reference-led recruiting brief on audience identification and immediate product clarity.

options.label: Monochrome marketing
options.risk: Clear but less aligned with the explicitly requested interaction identity.
options.case: Declined: weaker fit for this reference-led recruiting brief on audience identification and immediate product clarity.

options.label: Swiss poster grid
options.risk: Strong hierarchy, but a poster wall gives professional narrative less continuity.
options.case: Declined: weaker fit for this reference-led recruiting brief on audience identification and immediate product clarity.

options.label: Neon circuit
options.thesis: An illuminated path through product decisions
options.viewport: An illuminated path through product decisions
options.risk: Circuit controls and luminous lettering distract from readable professional evidence.
options.case: Declined: weaker fit for this reference-led recruiting brief on audience identification and immediate product clarity.

options.label: Provenance ribbon
options.thesis: Dated evidence along a continuous career line
options.viewport: Dated evidence along a continuous career line
options.risk: Chronology delays the strongest outcomes and immediate project access.
options.case: Declined: weaker fit for this reference-led recruiting brief on audience identification and immediate product clarity.

canonCard.label: Conventional portfolio
canonCard.thesis: A familiar professional introduction followed by project cards.
canonCard.viewport: Top navigation, name and summary, two direct actions, three outcome cards.
canonCard.risk: Easy to scan, but much less distinctive.
